title: Staging Payments to Your Contractor by Progress to Reduce Risk
desc: How to stage payments when building a house: advance amount, payment stages, retaining warranty money and documents per payment, with a sample schedule.
summary: Principles for staging payments to a contractor when building a house so money always follows work done, with a sample payment schedule and the documents needed for each payment.
body: p

The biggest risk in building a house is having paid money without matching work done: the contractor abandons the job, slows down or works carelessly, and the homeowner struggles to recover the money. Reasonable payment staging is the simplest and most effective protection.
h2
1. The law lets the two parties agree
p

The parties agree on the method, time, documents and conditions of payment and interim payment; the employer pays after deducting the advance payment and amounts retained as agreed (Clause 2, Article 87 of the Construction Law 2025). The advance level, number of advances and recovery level are also agreed by the parties (Clause 2, Article 12 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP); the form of payment is agreed by the parties (Clause 1, Article 28). The detailed levels in Decree 210 are mandatory only for state-funded and PPP projects; private homes may use them as a reference.
h2
2. Four principles to keep
ol
Money follows work: pay each installment only when the corresponding stage is complete and accepted.
An adequate but modest advance: an advance is interest-free money paid ahead so the contractor can mobilize (Clause 1, Article 12); it should not be large relative to the first portion of work.
Recover the advance gradually through the payment installments, stating the deduction rate for each installment.
Retain a portion until handover or the end of the warranty period, or replace it with a warranty guarantee if the two parties agree (Clause 2, Article 20).
h2
3. Sample payment schedule (for reference)
p

A hypothetical example for a lump-sum contract for a 3-floor townhouse. The percentages below are for illustration only and are not levels set by law; each building needs adjusting to actual quantities:
ol
Contract signing: 10% advance.
Foundation and underground tank done: 15% (gradually deducting the advance).
Frame and slabs of floors 1–2 done: 20%.
Frame and slabs of the remaining floors and the roof done: 20%.
Wall building, in-wall electrical and plumbing, and plastering done: 15%.
Finishing done, acceptance and handover: 15%.
Retain 5%: paid at the end of the agreed warranty period if there are no unremedied defects.
h2
4. What documents does each installment need?
p

The payment file is prepared by the contractor and confirmed by representatives of both parties; its components are agreed by the parties (Clause 1, Article 29). For a lump-sum contract, you can refer to the compact file set the Decree prescribes for state projects (Clause 2, Article 29):
ul
Minutes of acceptance of the quantities and work completed in the stage – see Acceptance of residential works.
A calculation of the value of work added outside the contract (if any).
A payment request stating: the value completed, additional work, the advance amount to be deducted, and the amount requested for this installment.
h2
5. Warning signs
ul
The contractor demands a large advance before starting, or demands the next installment before the previous stage is finished.
A request for cash payment with no signed receipt; prefer bank transfer and keep the records.
Actual work lags far behind the amount already paid.
p
When one party is late in paying, see Late payment under a construction contract: late-payment interest. If you need help preparing a payment schedule, you can contact Quan Construction.
note

This article is for reference only and is not financial or legal advice. The percentages in the sample schedule are hypothetical for illustration. The detailed provisions on advances, payment and documents in Decree 210/2026/ND-CP are mandatory only for state-funded and PPP projects; private housing contracts are agreed by the parties.
